original_statement: State equals reduce(log). Nothing exists that can't be rebuilt from log plus keys. Reducers are idempotent; convergence under reorder and duplication holds regardless of delivery order.
restatement: Client state must always be reconstructible from the log alone, with no hidden state and no sensitivity to delivery order: (s1) state derived by cold-start replay of the log always equals state maintained incrementally as events arrive; (s2) applying the same event twice never changes state beyond applying it once; (s3) any duplicated or reordered delivery of the same event set converges to identical state on every client, regardless of arrival order.

acceptance_tests.proves: Nothing exists in client state that the log can't rebuild — a cold-start replay always reproduces exactly the state built incrementally, across many randomized event sequences.
acceptance_tests.description: State derived by cold-start replay of the log always equals state maintained incrementally as events arrive.

acceptance_tests.proves: A reducer applied twice to the same event never drifts state further than applying it once, across many randomized event/state pairs — the idempotence at-least-once delivery depends on.
acceptance_tests.description: Applying the same event twice never changes state beyond applying it once — reducers are idempotent.

acceptance_tests.proves: Every explored delivery-order permutation and duplication of a fixed event set converges to the same canonical state hash — not just the one in-order, no-duplicates sequence a hand-written test would try.
acceptance_tests.description: Any duplicated or reordered delivery of the same event set converges to identical state on every client, regardless of arrival order.
